name: Tenzing and Random Operations
description: Yet another random problem. Tenzing has an array $$$a$$$ of length $$$n$$$ and an integer $$$v$$$. Tenzing will perform the following operation $$$m$$$ times: Choose an integer $$$i$$$ such that $$$1 \leq i \leq n$$$ uniformly at random. For all $$$j$$$ such that $$$i \leq j \leq n$$$, set $$$a_j := a_j + v$$$. Tenzing wants to know the expected value of $$$\prod_{i=1}^n a_i$$$ after performing the $$$m$$$ operations, modulo $$$10^9+7$$$. Formally, let $$$M = 10^9+7$$$. It can be shown that the answer can be expressed as an irreducible fraction $$$\frac{p}{q}$$$, where $$$p$$$ and $$$q$$$ are integers and $$$q \not \equiv 0 \pmod{M}$$$. Output the integer equal to $$$p \cdot q^{-1} \bmod M$$$. In other words, output the integer $$$x$$$ that $$$0 \le x \lt M$$$ and $$$x \cdot q \equiv p \pmod{M}$$$.
input_specification: The first line of input contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$1\leq n\leq 5000$$$, $$$1\leq m,v\leq 10^9$$$). The second line of input contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$$$ ($$$1\leq a_i\leq 10^9$$$).
output_specification: Output the expected value of $$$\prod_{i=1}^n a_i$$$ modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
approach_summary: Formulate expectation as E[X] = ∑ P(e) * v(e). Formulate linear transition equations on states and solve via DAG DP or Gaussian elimination.
